text:
IncidentsBot: Pager alert: streaming-pipeline-high-tail-latency triggered (p99 > 5s for SSE responses) — paging SRE-Oncall.

Alex: seeing big spike in p95/p99 for streaming responses to the public API (SSE). Dashboard shows p95 ~1.2s -> 3.5s, p99 ~2.6s -> 7.8s starting 12:07 UTC.

Maya: confirmed, traces show long gaps between chunks on the proxy side. A subset of clients stuck waiting for next chunk, connections not closing.

Julian: repro on staging with a long-running stream + small chunk sizes — proxy buffer growth then a timeout at upstream (~30s) when backpressure builds.

Priya: are we sure it's proxy buffering and not app-level stall? Logs show consistent token generation times from model pool.

Alex: stack trace/trace IDs attached in the dashboard link: https://redwood-infra/pipeline/traces/abc123 (FYI). Model gen is fine, proxy seems to be batching/chunking logic.

SRE-Oncall: quick mitigation checklist: 1) enable keepalive on proxy-client, 2) temporarily increase proxy chunk flush frequency, 3) apply per-connection rate limiting for noisy clients, 4) toggle upstream socket timeouts to be more forgiving. Working on 1 & 2 now.

Maya: deployed a config with flush_size -> 8KB and flush_interval -> 250ms to the canary proxy pool (proxy-canary-2).

IncidentsBot: Deploy started by Maya. Link: https://deploys/redwood/39823.

Julian: rolling restart proxies in the path for the affected region (us-east-1) to pick up config. Doing 5% at a time.

Alex: customer impact: ~22k requests in the last 15m saw > p99 latency; error rate hasn't spiked (0.2% -> 0.5%), most are slow rather than failed. Affected customers appear to be clients with long-polling SSE connections.

CustomerOps: flagged three paying customers in us-east region who reported degraded UX — CS ticket IDs: CS-8121, CS-8130, CS-8132. They are on legacy clients which may not honor keepalive.

Priya: adding a temporary mitigation at the routing layer: route legacy client IP ranges to dedicated proxies with relaxed backpressure (to avoid head-of-line blocking). Will add to routing rule in 5m.

Maya: canary shows immediate drop in tail latency for streams going through proxy-canary-2: p99 back to ~1.4s. Applying to another 20% now.

SRE-Oncall: good. Also enabling short-term circuit-breaker: if stream hasn't emitted a chunk in 15s, proxy will send a heartbeat chunk to keep client alive. This should reduce perceived stalls.

Alex: added a guard in our streaming SDK docs to encourage clients to support chunk heartbeats and exponential reconnect. Post link in thread for customers.

Julian: note from traces — some clients send TCP window size 0 briefly; looks like client-side backpressure is exacerbating server proxy batching. Recommend CustomerOps reach out to the three flagged customers with suggested client update.

CustomerOps: noted, preparing outreach with suggested changes (enable keepalives, update to SDK v2.4.1). Will also offer to test in a staging env.

Priya: routing change applied to legacy IP ranges, traffic shifted to dedicated proxies with new chunking config. Monitoring.

Maya: full rollout of the new proxy config to us-east completed at 12:43 UTC. p95/p99 trending down: p95 ~0.9s, p99 ~1.6s.

Alex: telemetry note: we should add a new metric for 'time-between-chunks' per connection to catch this earlier. Filed infra ticket INF-5494.

Julian: leaving a note — we saw a pattern: small-chunk, long-live streams + clients that throttle reads => proxy buffer growth => upstream socket timeout. Remediation paths: tweak flush interval, send heartbeats, and client-side fixes.

SRE-Oncall: investigating whether proxy version 3.2.1 has a regression in flush heuristics; running bisect on the canary.

Maya: canary bisect indicates change in 3.2.1 that reduces eager flush under certain TLS record sizes. Rolling back that specific change in 3.2.2 patch being tested now.

IncidentsBot: Alert update: streaming-pipeline-high-tail-latency resolved for us-east.

Alex: impact summary to include in postmortem: root cause (proxy flush heuristics + client backpressure), mitigations (config changes, routing for legacy clients, heartbeat chunk, rollback patch), customer impact (slow only, minor error increase, three flagged customers with degraded UX), follow-ups (INF-5494 telemetry, SDK client note, proxy 3.2.2 patch release).

Priya: handing over to next oncall for follow-ups. @SRE-Oncall will add handoff info.

SRE-Oncall: Handoff -> Next on-call: Maya will be primary for next 12h for watch and final validation. I created an oncall-handoff note: https://oncall/redwood/handoffs/1742500001.

Maya: I'll monitor dashboards and customer tickets for the next 6 hours. If something regresses we'll re-open the page.

Alex: thanks team. Adding incident label: "streaming-tail-latency-mitigation" and starting a short postmortem draft.

CustomerOps: customers notified with workaround and staging test offer. Closing loop when PMs confirm no regression on their end. :white_check_mark:

IncidentsBot: Thread closed by SRE-Oncall.
